summary: Ten comment-endorsed finds spanning developer tools, design, privacy, retro hardware, and interactive fiction.
telegram_footer: 10 items surfaced | 30/30 HN /front stories processed | history + run artifact updated

items.name: xc
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Ledge.sh – Runnable Markdown Notes
items.summary: Markdown task runner; a long-term user runs home-infrastructure deployments from README files.
items.why_included: A long-term user directly praises its reliability and describes a concrete deployment workflow.
items.evidence: 20after4 calls xc fairly solid after long-term use and says they use it to deploy router, firewall, DNS, and container changes from a README.

evidence_sources.author: 20after4
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've used xc³ for a long time now and it's fairly solid.

items.name: Org Babel
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Ledge.sh – Runnable Markdown Notes
items.summary: Emacs notebook system combining executable code, research notes, plots, and PDF exports.
items.why_included: Concrete research use is backed by an independent comment praising the runnable notebooks.
items.evidence: mfld describes combining data-wrangling code, plots, and notes and exporting PDFs for collaborators; mijoharas praises the runnable notebooks.

evidence_sources.author: mfld
evidence_sources.excerpt: During my time as a researcher, I heavily used org-babel. I used it to put code for data wrangling, plots, and notes into a single document.

evidence_sources.author: mijoharas
evidence_sources.excerpt: org-babel (which can make some very nice runnable notebooks)

items.name: egui
items.source_story_title: How to speed up the Rust compiler in September 2026
items.summary: Cross-platform Rust GUI library; a desktop-app developer praises it after leaving Tauri.
items.why_included: A developer explicitly endorses the library after switching their desktop applications to it.
items.evidence: echelon says they stopped using Tauri for egui and calls it cross-platform and excellent, with attractive results when given design constraints.

evidence_sources.author: echelon
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've stopped using Tauri and gone with 100% egui. It's cross platform and excellent, and if you give it design constraints it will look beautiful.

items.name: OpenPencil
items.source_story_title: Figma restricts MCP access to whitelisted clients, excluding Pi
items.summary: Open-source design editor; a Figma user reports it works as their replacement.
items.why_included: The endorsement is a concrete first-hand replacement report rather than launch promotion.
items.evidence: sneezychl says they have been using OpenPencil as a drop-in Figma replacement and that it works fine for their needs.

evidence_sources.author: sneezychl
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've been using OpenPencil as a drop-in replacement for Figma and it works fine for my needs.

items.name: Book of Shapes
items.source_story_title: Book of Shapes – Collection of minimal, generative and customizable SVG-patterns
items.summary: Customizable generative SVG-pattern collection; a commenter explicitly praises its visual quality.
items.why_included: An independent comment directly endorses the collection's appearance.
items.evidence: loclol101 calls the submitted collection amazing and beautiful.

items.name: Adam Fuhrer
items.source_story_title: Book of Shapes – Collection of minimal, generative and customizable SVG-patterns
items.summary: Algorithmic-art gallery featuring pen plots, digital patterns, and experimental hardware pieces.
items.why_included: A commenter explicitly praises the named artist's visual work and links the portfolio.
items.evidence: kachnuv_ocasek calls Adam Fuhrer's visual art amazing while discussing generative patterns.

evidence_sources.author: kachnuv_ocasek
evidence_sources.excerpt: Reminds me of the amazing visual art of Adam Fuhrer[1].

items.name: StrongPhrase.net
items.source_story_title: Cops Can Bypass iPhone's Automatic Reboot to Get into Locked Phones
items.summary: Random-passphrase generator recommended for memorable phrases in a phone-security discussion.
items.why_included: The commenter explicitly recommends the generator's memorable output, not merely its domain.
items.evidence: Cider9986 links StrongPhrase.net as a source of memorable random passphrases and calls that quality cool.

evidence_sources.author: Cider9986
evidence_sources.excerpt: https://strongphrase.net give memorable ones which is cool.

items.name: The Wise-Woman's Dog
items.summary: Bronze Age interactive fiction; a player praises its historical texture and footnotes.
items.why_included: A player endorses both the experience and its ability to make the historical setting vivid.
items.evidence: kqr describes learning about ordinary Bronze Age life through the game, highlights its footnotes, and calls it fun and useful for bringing the period alive.

evidence_sources.author: kqr
evidence_sources.excerpt: It's made by someone who researches that sort of thing for a living, and is full of interesting footnotes too. It's a fun experience and a useful way to make a place and a time really feel alive.

items.name: Internet History Roulette
items.summary: Early-web time machine serving random archived pages; watch for fast-changing fact bubbles.
items.why_included: A commenter directly recommends it for exploring sites from the dial-up era.
items.evidence: adrianwaj recommends the site for seeing pages from that era, while noting that its optional fact bubbles change too quickly.

evidence_sources.author: adrianwaj
evidence_sources.excerpt: To see sites from back then checkout: https://internethistoryroulette.com/ - could be improved whereby the "facts" bubbles change too quickly when turned on.

items.name: Lectron
items.summary: Vintage magnetic electronics-building kit; an admired modular-design rabbit hole, now second-hand.
items.why_included: A commenter explicitly likes the named physical system and points readers toward surviving kits.
items.evidence: frnz says they like the Lectron system and suggests searching eBay for Braun Lectron kits.

evidence_sources.author: frnz
evidence_sources.excerpt: I also like this LECTRON-system by Gregor Greger from 1965.
